description: Environment contract between the warp-server dispatch path and the Warp client for Agent Plugins in a file-managed Factory run. warp-server asserts the producing half against this file; the Warp client vendors a verbatim copy and asserts the consuming half, so a divergence appears as a diff between two committed files.

environment_variables.name: WARP_SKILL_DIRS
environment_variables.order: most specific first: agent, then factory

environment_variables.name: WARP_PLUGIN_DIRS
environment_variables.order: most specific first: automation, then bound agent, then factory
environment_variables.notes: Each entry is a plugin collection directory. The client enumerates immediate child directories as packages; a package whose manifest name repeats in a later directory is shadowed by the earlier one.

environment_variables.name: WARP_FACTORY_MCP_FILES
environment_variables.order: most specific first: automation, then bound agent, then factory
environment_variables.notes: The client loads ordinary entries and ignores managed entries, which Factory sync already projected.

environment_variables.name: WARP_FACTORY_UID
environment_variables.notes: Identity and diagnostics only. It is never used to compose a path: the plugin data root already carries it.

environment_variables.name: WARP_PLUGIN_DATA_ROOT
environment_variables.notes: Absence means the backend has no durable storage, and the client must not start a Factory plugin stdio MCP server.

invariants: Exactly two segments below the root. Neither may contain a path separator, and neither may be '.' or '..'.
Nothing below the root mentions the Factory UID: it appears exactly once in a composed path, in the root the server exported.
The scope segment is flat, never nested: an agent contributes one segment, not agent/<name>.
notes: The Factory UID is baked into the exported root by the server so two Factories running as the same principal cannot share a data directory.

Agent, automation, and manifest names are author-controlled and become directory segments, so the client sanitizes them before joining. For a conformant package the plugin key is a no-op: Agent Plugins 5.5 already restricts a manifest name to lowercase alphanumerics, hyphens, and periods.
The client keeps its own local layout (plugins/data/<hash>) for non-Factory plugins; this contract governs Factory plugins only.

sanitize.description: Maps an author-controlled name to a single safe path segment. It is total: every input produces a usable segment.
steps: 1. Map each character: keep [a-z0-9._-], lowercase A-Z, replace everything else with '-'.
2. If the mapped result is byte-identical to the input AND is not '', '.' or '..', return it unchanged.

3. Otherwise compute SHA-256 over the ORIGINAL input bytes and take the first 4 bytes as 8 lowercase hex characters. For an empty or reserved mapped result return the hex alone; otherwise return '<mapped>-<hex>'.
porting_traps: The digest is computed over the ORIGINAL input, not over the mapped result. Hashing the mapped form is easy to do by accident and silently resolves the same name to a different directory.

'..' survives step 1 byte-identical, so the did-it-change test does not catch it. It must be caught by the explicit reserved check. A port that only compares mapped-against-input reintroduces path traversal exactly here.
sanitize.examples_provenance: Every entry in sanitize_examples was produced by executing an implementation of the rule, not written by hand. Verify a port by reproducing all of them; a port that matches the prose but not these outputs is wrong.

sanitize_examples.why: separator replaced, so the digest is appended
uppercase lowercased and space replaced, so the digest is appended
empty result, so the digest alone
reserved result, so the digest alone
reserved result caught by the reserved check rather than the changed check, so the digest alone
separators replaced while periods are kept, so the digest is appended; the result is one segment with no separator and is not '..', so traversal is neutralized

examples.why: a hostile agent name still yields exactly two segments below the root
